incumbent.name: Travis Holdman
incumbent.summary: Sen. Travis Holdman (R-Markle), in the Senate since 2008, majority caucus chair and chair of the Tax and Fiscal Policy Committee, lost the May 2026 Republican primary to Trump-endorsed challenger Blake Fiechter after voting against the December 2025 congressional redistricting plan {holdman_bio} {cr_primary} {icc_trump_holdman}.
record: 2025: Authored Senate Bill 1, the Senate Republicans' property-tax bill, which the caucus says provides about $1.3 billion in relief over three years, including a homestead credit of 10% up to $300, and lowers the local income tax cap from 3.75% to 2.9% {holdman_sb1} {holdman_bio}.

Dec. 11, 2025: Was one of 21 Republicans who joined all 10 Democrats to defeat the mid-decade congressional redistricting plan 31–19; in November he had said his district did not support mid-cycle redistricting {icc_trump_holdman}.

Feb. 2026: Authored SEA 243, which, according to the Senate Republican caucus, aligns Indiana's tax code with federal tax provisions on tips, overtime, and interest on loans for American-made vehicles for tax year 2026 {holdman_sea243}.
Jan. 2026: President Trump called Holdman a 'RINO' in a social media post and endorsed Fiechter; Holdman did not respond to the Indiana Capital Chronicle's requests for comment {icc_trump_holdman}.

race_context: Senate District 19 covers all of Jay, Blackford, Wells, and Adams counties and the southwest corner of Allen County {cr_primary} {holdman_bio}.

This is an open seat: incumbent Travis Holdman lost the May 5, 2026 Republican primary to Bluffton City Council member Blake Fiechter, 8,449 votes (61.4%) to 5,312 in unofficial results reported by The Commercial Review {cr_primary}. Wikipedia's results compilation lists 8,684 (61.5%) to 5,441 {wiki_2026_insen}.

President Trump targeted Holdman after his vote against the December 2025 redistricting bill; political action committees spent heavily on ads against Holdman, and Fiechter said the outside spending muddied the race but raised his name recognition {cr_primary}. WANE reported that super PACs tied to Sen. Jim Banks and Gov. Mike Braun and allied groups spent more than $8.3 million across seven such Senate primaries, according to AdImpact {wane_primary}.
Democrat Timothy C. Murphy was unopposed in the primary {cr_primary}.
No debate or forum between Fiechter and Murphy was found in available coverage.

The candidates' published platforms differ on taxes (Fiechter calls for cutting government spending and reforming property-tax laws; Murphy proposes progressive income and property taxes), abortion, and labor law {fiechter_site} {murphy_platform}.

candidates.summary: Blake Fiechter is a real estate broker and first-term Bluffton City Council member who defeated Sen. Travis Holdman in the May 2026 Republican primary after President Trump endorsed him {icc_trump_holdman} {cr_primary}.
background: A real estate broker in his first term as an at-large Bluffton City Council member, elected in 2023 {icc_trump_holdman}.
His campaign says he is a small business owner, serves on a local redevelopment commission, and is a third-generation Bluffton resident {fiechter_site}.
path_to_ballot: Trump endorsed Fiechter on Jan. 22, 2026, before Fiechter had filed for the seat {icc_trump_holdman}.
WANE reported he announced in February that he was stepping away from the race, then reversed that decision; WANE also reported endorsements from Trump and Gov. Mike Braun {wane_primary}.
Won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary with 61.4% in unofficial results, including Jay County (1,633 to 1,136), and did best in Adams County (65.5%) {cr_primary}.

items: His campaign says he would address high costs for groceries, gas, and utilities by cutting government spending {fiechter_site}.
On primary night he said he wants to bring relief from rising expenses and 'fresh perspectives' to the Senate {wboi_primary}.
His campaign pledges to reform property-tax laws so families and seniors are not forced out of their homes {fiechter_site}.
His campaign says rural communities and farmers should be heard and receive their fair share of state funding {fiechter_site}.
His campaign describes him as pro-life {fiechter_site}.
His campaign says he would oppose efforts to restrict firearms and protect Second Amendment rights {fiechter_site}.
His campaign says he supports term limits for elected officials {fiechter_site}.

on_incumbent: On primary night he thanked Holdman for his years of service {wboi_primary}.
plans: His campaign lists cutting government spending, property-tax reform, and term limits among his goals {fiechter_site}.
endorsements_finance: Endorsed by President Trump and, per WANE, Gov. Mike Braun {icc_trump_holdman} {wane_primary}.
The Commercial Review reported Holdman's campaign outraised Fiechter's in the primary, while outside PACs ran ads against Holdman {cr_primary}.
gaps: Search snippets said the Indiana Capital Chronicle voter guide quoted his site as '100% pro-life, from conception to natural death' and that he did not respond to the Chronicle's survey; the guide returned 403.
Wikipedia lists additional endorsements (Sen. Jim Banks, Rep. Erin Houchin, Turning Point Action, Indiana Farm Bureau AgELECT PAC post-primary); not verified on a primary source.
No general-election fundraising totals found; the state campaign finance portal was not reviewed.
No general-election interviews or Q&As found; search budget ran out before further searches.

candidates.summary: Timothy C. Murphy is a pastor running for office for the first time who was unopposed for the Democratic nomination {murphy_about} {cr_primary}.
background: According to his campaign, he is the pastor of a local church, grew up in Kentucky, and has lived in Fort Wayne since 2018 {murphy_about}.
His campaign says this is his first run for office {murphy_about}.
path_to_ballot: Unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary {cr_primary}.

items: His platform proposes a citizen-led ballot initiative process and multi-member districts with proportional representation {murphy_platform}.
His platform proposes replacing Indiana's flat income tax with a progressive income tax and establishing a progressive property tax {murphy_platform}.
His platform proposes raising the minimum wage with inflation indexing, repealing right-to-work, and tax incentives for businesses that put workers on their boards {murphy_platform}.
It also calls for subsidized child care of no more than $10 per child per day, at least 13 weeks of paid parental leave, and at least five paid sick days a year {murphy_platform}.
His platform calls for spending transparency for charter and private schools that receive public funds {murphy_platform}.
His platform calls for billing transparency, expanded access in every county, protecting Medicaid eligibility, and restoring abortion access {murphy_platform}.
His platform calls for stronger air- and water-quality rules and expanded battery storage and transmission for clean energy {murphy_platform}.
His platform calls for stronger tenant rights, community land trusts, and more affordable units in tax-advantaged public-private projects {murphy_platform}.

on_incumbent: No statements by Murphy about Holdman, Fiechter, or the seat's record were found; his platform says the economic and political system 'does not work for most people' {murphy_platform}.
plans: His platform also proposes more bus funding with free rides for riders under 18 and over 65 {murphy_platform}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements are listed on his campaign site {murphy_home}.
gaps: No news coverage of Murphy beyond primary-result mentions was found.
No fundraising totals found; the state campaign finance portal was not reviewed.
Whether his Fort Wayne residence is within the district's Allen County portion was not verified.
